executiveSummary: GM0797's 2025 identity, boundary, population, neighbourhood, place, settlement and safety-region inputs reconcile exactly, and the deterministic gate covers all ten canonical presets, six checkpoints and eight services. River flooding is genuinely material: Heusden lies by the Maas/Bergsche Maas, official planning identifies higher over-20-cm flood probability along the river and Drongelens Kanaal, Howabo links Maas backwater with Aa/Dommel/Dieze discharge and storage, and the Doeveren defence is being improved because it no longer meets current standards. That supports eligibility, not the model's precise 1.933193 normalized inundation stress, 31,707 affected people-equivalent at T+72 or one frozen municipal service trajectory: no selected hydrograph, defence/breach/control state, connected LIWO footprint, depth, arrival or recession drives it. Eight unrelated hazards reuse exactly the same complete 17-neighbourhood order. A controlled source in official Venne-Oost/TOP10NL woodland at the Loonse en Drunense Duinen edge yields direct fire 0.321928 and smoke 0.458454, yet Venne-Oost ranks 15/17. The three-edge A59/N267 graph and bus schedule omit internal crossings, the Heusdense bridge, water-storage compartments, acute-care transfers and response/supply access. Heusden has no acute hospital: JBZ confirms its Drunen location has no ED and the 24/7 ED is in 's-Hertogenbosch; ETZ Waalwijk also has no ED. Public water assets, Heesbeen observations/forecasts, grid planning, antennas, schools and preparedness guidance are valuable dated context but not live topology, capacity, occupancy, backup, route state or recovery. Retain official geography, directional flood/fire eligibility and arithmetic; suppress exact local consequence, access, outage and recovery claims unless publisher, version, issue/valid time, coverage, licence, evidence class and Unknown/NoData are explicit.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0797 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; CBS/PDOK inputs retrieved 31 August 2026; BRT settlement snapshot retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0797 as Heusden and reports 46,365 residents, density 588/km², 22.4% aged 65 or older and 6,294 one-person households; the generated centre is inside the 2025 boundary.

All seventeen published neighbourhood rows sum exactly to 46,365 residents; households sum to 20,280 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 10,390. Deterministic allocation preserves the official municipality total.

Eleven active BAG woonplaatsen are Doeveren, Drunen, Elshout, Haarsteeg, Hedikhuizen, Heesbeen, Herpt, Heusden, Nieuwkuijk, Oudheusden and Vlijmen. BRT supplies sixteen settlement labels: eleven woonkernen, three deelkernen, one buurtschap and one gehucht.

CBS neighbourhoods and registered residents are annual administrative context, not flood compartments, dune/forest cells, service zones or event-time people. BAG/PDOK place data carries Public Domain Mark 1.0; null, suppressed and not-applicable values remain NoData.

evidenceSources.title: Waterplan Heusden — Programma Water en Riolering 2023-2027
evidenceSources.edition: Plan dated 20 July 2022 for 2023-2027; current funding update inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The plan reports about 360 km of sewer pipes: 186 km mixed, 33 km foul-water, 38 km stormwater, 9 km other gravity pipe, 69 km pressure sewer and 15 km force main, plus 63 main pumps, 350 pressure units, six retention facilities, 42 unbuffered combined-sewer overflows, 61 stormwater outlets, twenty infiltration facilities and thirty special stormwater features.

It records that large areas flooded during extreme rain on 16 June 2020 and 10 September 2021, specifically illustrating Nieuwkuijk, Vlijmen/Vliedberg and Drunen. It attributes vulnerability to increased paving, drowned sewer overflows and more extreme rain.

The SSW used 70 mm in one hour as a stress-test criterion; the municipality aims to keep buildings dry while accepting that some public space may be temporarily unusable. That design/ambition is not an observed event, guaranteed protection or current passability layer.

The plan says real-time water control and a calamity/incident plan were still being developed and lists dangerous discharge, prolonged pump failure, force-main break, main-sewer collapse under a key road and extreme rain as incident classes. Narrative/inventory evidence has no live state or blanket open-data licence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Heusden / Waterschap Aa en Maas / Waterschap De Dommel / Rijkswaterstaat / Provincie Noord-Brabant
evidenceSources.title: Howabo high-water system, Heusden environmental baseline and proposed measures
evidenceSources.edition: Current Howabo page and April 2026 draft programme; municipal environmental baseline dated 12 July 2022
supports: The municipality says low-lying Heusden and 's-Hertogenbosch have comparatively high flood exposure where Maas levels interact with Aa, Dommel and Dieze discharge; consequences can include flooded homes, unusable roads and inaccessible hospitals.

The 2022 baseline maps place-specific probability of more than 20 cm by 2050: medium probability along the southern Drongelens Kanaal and greater probability along Maas/Bergsche Maas. It distinguishes Vlijmen-area storage and A59 compartment changes from river-defence measures.

The April 2026 draft Howabo programme proposes eleven measures and 36 million m³ storage. Crèvecoeur closes when the Maas is high, shifting Aa/Dommel discharge toward Drongelens Kanaal; proposed pumps, storage in Engelermeer/Bossche Broek/Bokhovense Polder and other works have sequencing and location choices.

A planning probability map and draft programme establish mechanisms and candidate actions, not a selected incident hydrograph, current defence state, commissioned storage, live road state or exact municipal depth/recovery. No reusable operational raster licence/cadence was stated.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Aa en Maas / Het Waterschapshuis / Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: Doeveren defence, Drongelens Kanaal control, IMWA/DAMO assets and Waterinfo evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Doeveren final decision September 2025 and construction update December 2025; public snapshots retrieved 2-3 September 2026
supports: Aa en Maas says the 4.1 km defence between N267 at Heusden and Drongelens Kanaal no longer meets safety requirements; construction was scheduled from summer 2026 toward a future-safe 2027 result. This is neither proof of present failure nor completed protection.

The water board says the Bovenlandse Sluis regulates Drongelens Kanaal discharge to Bergsche Maas and supplies the Vlijmen/Drunen polders; a March 2026 fault/leak inspection and planned maintenance demonstrate event- and asset-state dependence.

The partial national CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH aggregation assigns 94 points to GM0797: 69 weirs, eleven surface-water pumps, eight sluices and six sewer pumps. Contributor completeness varies; records and capacity fields do not establish connectivity, compatible units, current operation, power/backup or restoration.

The CC0 Waterinfo snapshot has one fresh Heesbeen observation, 36 cm NAP at 17:30 UTC on 2 September, and rolling forecasts classed normal at requested T+1/6/12/24/48 with values 39/37/44/56/68 cm NAP; no T+72 point is returned. The public frontend is not mission-critical/stable, point/class is not a flood surface or defence state, and absent T+72 is NoData, never zero.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Brabant-Noord / Provincie Noord-Brabant / Brandweer Nederland
evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2024-2027 and Loonse en Drunense Duinen nature-fire context
evidenceSources.edition: Regional profile version 8 June 2023, adopted 30 November 2023 for 2024-2027; nature-fire memo March 2023; Natura 2000 plan validity extended January 2025
supports: The regional profile retains flood, extreme-weather, nature-fire, dangerous-goods and vital-service scenarios as preparedness cases and explicitly notes that electricity/telecom/drinking-water/energy partner systems cross administrative boundaries. A regional scenario is not a Heusden event or local probability.

VRBN's nature-fire memo names a Loonse en Drunense Duinen area commission with a direct relationship to Heusden and Vught and describes increasing Mediterranean-like fire danger. It is preparedness context, not current incident severity or resource availability.

The province describes the nearly 4,000 ha Natura 2000 complex as one of western Europe's largest drifting-sand areas, surrounded by deciduous and coniferous forest, with dry nutrient-poor soil and significant recreation. Static habitat/planning evidence does not supply live fuel, moisture, visitors, ignition, perimeter, smoke or suppression.

Current nature-fire phase is independently time-varying and region-wide. A phase value cannot be generalized to a specific cell, and a current low phase would not validate a historical/synthetic scenario. Narrative sources expose no complete machine update/licence/NoData contract.

evidenceSources.edition: TOP10NL feature d584a33f-dc7c-505e-b33d-bebea8531c22; source actuality 1 January 2010 and registration 23 October 2011

The point lies in the official Heusden/Loonse en Drunense Duinen context supported by E05, making it suitable for a synthetic containment regression but not an operational incident.

The province identifies the N267/Heusdense bridge and current Kromme Nol/Heesbeenseweg junction constraints; project alternatives are future planning, not present incident passability. Municipal evidence identifies A59/N267 as primary access and dangerous-goods routes.

No ProRail station is inside GM0797; the municipal baseline says all public transport is by bus and generally weak outside cores. GTFS version 9543 supplies sixty stop areas, not live vehicles, passengers, accessibility, evacuation throughput or restoration.
Zero covered CC0 NDW current situations is no matching usable record at publication time, not proof that A59, N267/Heusdense bridge, local water crossings, bus routes or emergency access are open.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning stress test, not a KNMI, WMCN/LIWO, Aa en Maas, De Dommel, RWS, VRBN, municipality, hospital or operator warning, forecast, probability, evacuation order, casualty model or restoration commitment.
No expert-selected Heusden Maas/Bergsche Maas, Heusdensch/Drongelens canal, Howabo, regional-water, groundwater, sewer or pluvial event with connected footprint drives the simulation.

The current river field is normalized inundation stress in a legacy floodDepthM field, not verified metres; source, hydrograph/datum, defence/control, arrival, velocity, duration/recession, resolution, units, coverage, NoData, uncertainty and layer licence are absent.
Howabo's probability/context and proposed 36-million-m³ programme do not identify a current event or commissioned protection; draft/proposed measures remain future state.

Doeveren's noncompliance and current construction do not mean immediate failure, while its target 2027 improvement is not completed protection. Scenario-time condition remains Unknown without owner evidence.

The municipal SSW/Waterplan identifies 70-mm design assumptions, historic hotspots and system totals but is not an event-valid reusable depth raster or live sewer model; unavailable cells/technical metadata remain Unknown.
CBS generalized polygons and labels do not resolve terrain, flood compartments, defenses, storage, sewers, buildings, paving, shade, woodland, facilities, crossings or household exposure.
CBS values are rounded/suppressed; district heating and charging are absent everywhere and cars per household is missing once. Null is Unknown, never zero service, demand or safety.
Registered residents omit patients/staff, care-home residents, workers, pupils, bus passengers, tourists, dune visitors and responders; no authorized event-time transient ledger is available.

TOP10NL Venne-Oost woodland is old/static eligibility only; the focused ignition is synthetic and no live fuel, moisture, perimeter, wind, access, firewater, visitor occupancy or suppression state is available.

Static NWB and GTFS geometry/schedules do not establish live A59/N267/Heusdense bridge/local crossing/bus, evacuation, emergency-priority or freight state/capacity; east/west A59 edges are one non-additive corridor.
Zero covered NDW situations is no usable record at publication time, not proof roads or crossings are open. Flood-driven local failures can fall outside that snapshot.

HWH asset points and project/inventory pages do not establish complete defence/water/wastewater topology, compatible capacity units, control logic, operation, power backup, staff or repair; missing values/assets are Unknown.

The Heesbeen observation and T+1/6/12/24/48 forecasts are dated normal-class local points from a non-mission-critical/undocumented frontend, not a municipal surface, defence threshold, breach scenario or operating instruction; absent T+72 is NoData.

No complete public physical Enexis feeder/switching, Brabant Water pipe/pressure/quality, gas district/valve, telecom backhaul or sewer topology is authorized in the model; one postcode sample is planning context only.

Zero RIVM acute-care points inside Heusden is correct questionnaire geography but not zero care need. JBZ Drunen and ETZ Waalwijk have no ED; external capacity is dated, not live acceptance, staffing, occupancy, medicine/oxygen, generator/fuel or restoration.

RDI and DUO points identify registered installation/use, not communications coverage, reception activation, people present, capacity, supplies, power backup or recovery; RDI reuse terms are unresolved.
Dangerous-goods road/site presence does not imply a release. No current material, containment, plume/water pathway, firefighting-water, shutdown or restart state drives the model.
Cyber disruption has no named target, architecture, attack/detection/containment state or authoritative operational evidence; generic service loss is not an observed incident.

Preparedness guidance does not measure household readiness or identify activated support/reception points. No validated public inventory exists for pumps/generators, fuel, food/water/medicine stocks, crews, vehicles, mutual aid or completed actions.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not customer outage-hours, injuries, mortality, evacuation, displacement or welfare loss; 72 hours excludes weeks-long flooding and reconstruction.
